correctness.rationale: A free amalgam of Fano-free hypergraphs stays Fano-free because a forbidden copy covers every pair, including any pair on opposite sides. The extension property and homogeneity identify types outside the named base with legal links; repeated free amalgamation gives infinitely many realizations. Deleting the new point from a forbidden copy leaves four old Pasch triples, and the deleted lines require exactly the three opposite pairs in the link. In a PSTS, write the four triples as ace, adf, bcf, bde. A common opposite pair ab and an extra common point c determine e and f via the unique completions of ac and bc; the unique completion of af now forces d. Hence distinct Pasches with a shared opposite pair have exactly two old vertices in common, requiring ten old vertices, and their matchings intersect in only one bit. The one-event fraction is 7/8. Two events have intersection 2^-5 or 2^-6, leaving 25/32 or 49/64. The link consisting just of the three coordinates of a third distinct clause witnesses strict further loss. In the ten-point witness both sides have pair-unique triples; no pair between exclusive vertices is covered, so no Fano copy crosses sides. Any mixed Pasch would have to have all four triples through the same attachment point, inconsistent with Pasch degrees. The five constrained bits give 25 times 2^40 legal links. Disjoint or isolated padding gives the remaining stated witnesses, including 7 times 2^12 on six points. Independent finite enumeration corroborated the ten-point witness; the arguments, not the enumeration, prove the universal bounds.
residual_risks: Does not assert sharpness of 49/64 separately at every order from six to nine, or a count determined solely by the number of Pasches.

originality.rationale: The compared literature covers the Fano deletion geometry and PSTS pair-uniqueness, while the closest indexed counts impose a different extension condition, a different forbidden configuration, or a different number of new points. No compared statement gives the named-base PSTS overlap rigidity together with the sharp first and second type-count losses. This is a best-of-knowledge assessment, not a historical priority determination.
residual_risks: A focused general literature lookup was unavailable; this is not a negative result. A prior equivalent overlap lemma under quadrilateral or trade terminology is possible. No exhaustive design enumeration or historical priority claim is made.

value.rationale: The count measures restrictions on free one-point extension in a natural forbidden-design age. The second obstruction is not just a repeated first penalty: the exact maximal surviving fraction changes with a specific overlap that is geometrically impossible below ten vertices, and the theorem characterizes equality and supplies a minimal witness. That distinction is useful in comparing extension spectra; the contribution is not just a small-instance count.
residual_risks: No claim that higher-order interactions follow only from the number of Pasches, or that the rigidity extends to arbitrary Fano-free old bases.
